maria_sales: Hey team — FinRegCo wants a POC with a 'hot standby' across EU + APAC. Main constraint: all production traffic should prefer EU (data residency), but they want automatic failover to APAC only during regional outage. They also want: 1) precise routing policy example we can show to them, 2) list of APAC subprocessors that would touch data during failover, 3) high-level pricing delta for cross-region egress during failover, and 4) confirmation KMS keys can stay in EU and how KMS routing works when we fail over. Need answers for security questionnaire by EOD Friday — can ops/infra/security help?

alex_infra: cc @jordan_sre @sam_security — short answer: yes we can do EU-preferred with APAC fallback. But there are caveats on sticky sessions and KV cache warmup.

alex_infra: Example policy (simplified):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  primary_region: eu-west-1
  fallback_regions: [ap-southeast-1]
  failover_condition: region_unavailable
  max_reroute_latency_ms: 200
  require_customer_approval_for_data_move: true
  audit: enabled
```

alex_infra: Important notes:
- During failover we serve from APAC which may change jurisdiction for ephemeral logs/metrics.
- KV cache and batching effectiveness will drop for cold-started APAC workers. Expect ~2-3x token cost for a short window.

jordan_sre: Ops checklist for the POC:
- Run chaosmonkey network partition test to validate failover.
- Validate sticky routing TTL (we use 30s by default, can increase to 2m).
- Estimate bandwidth: assume baseline 1TB/month, worst-case full-failover egress to APAC ~ additional 0.8TB/month (depends on request distribution).

jordan_sre: For SLOs: we can keep latency SLOs if customer accepts ~50ms extra median once cache is warmed on APAC. If they need identical latency, need dedicated APAC warm standby (higher cost).

sam_security: Re: subprocessors — APAC failover uses these cloud zones/providers:
- ap-southeast-1: GCP (listed subprocessor: GCP Compute Engine)
- ap-northeast-1: AWS (EC2, EBS, optional S3)
- local logging/monitoring: Datadog EU+APAC (we control retention region)
I will attach the formal subprocessor inventory to the questionnaire answers.

sam_security: KMS note: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) pinned to eu-west-1. During failover we will route requests to APAC but KMS operations can still be proxied to EU KMS endpoints (adds latency and egress). If customer requires keys to never leave EU, we must ensure envelope encryption where only ciphertext leaves region; plaintext unwrapped only in EU KMS (we can implement).

maria_sales: Helpful, thanks. Need a short one-paragraph explanation for the security questionnaire that I can paste into the doc (covering routing, subprocessors, KMS behavior, and audit logs). Can someone draft?

sam_security: Draft for questionnaire (paste-ready):
"Redwood will implement an EU-preferred routing policy for the FinRegCo POC. Production requests are routed to EU-only compute under normal operation. APAC regions are configured as automatic failover targets and will only serve traffic if EU compute is unavailable — all failover events are recorded in audit logs and require customer notification. Subprocessors used in APAC during failover are standard cloud compute and monitoring providers (GCP/AWS) and are listed in our subprocessor inventory; we will provide the exact list in the questionnaire. Customer-managed keys (BYOK) can be pinned to EU KMS; during APAC failover we proxy KMS unwrap operations back to EU KMS to avoid key material leaving the EU. All data movements and KMS operations are logged and retained per the agreed retention policy."

alex_infra: Pricing delta quick estimate for sales: if failover traffic is infrequent (<5% of traffic), egress delta is negligible — we bill actual cross-region egress + small routing surcharge (~$0.02/GB in this POC estimate). For sustained failover (full region down), expect egress and compute cost increase roughly +20-40% depending on cache effectiveness.

maria_sales: Great. Can we get the subprocessor inventory and the formal cost estimate as a PDF by Thursday? Also need ops runbook for the failover test.

jordan_sre: I'll produce runbook steps + chaos test commands by Thu morning. Quick runbook snippet for POC test:
```bash
# simulate eu-west outage
kubectl cordon -n Redwood eu-workers && sleep 60
# observe routing reassignments in the console
redwoodctl routing status --tenant finregco
```

deploy-bot: deploy 2468-hot-standby-proto -> staging succeeded :white_check_mark: (tag: p〇c-hot-standby)

maria_sales: Perfect. Thanks everyone — I'll send the questionnaire draft + policy YAML to FinRegCo and flag follow-ups. If anything else pops up, ping in this thread. :pray:
